title: Shards versus replicas
description: Separate dataset ownership from redundant copies.

steps.title: Route one key
steps.description: The example range map sends order 42 to shard A. A request for order 142 would go to shard B.

steps.title: Split rows across shards
steps.description: The two primaries own disjoint order ranges. Adding a shard can add capacity, but requires a plan to redistribute rows.

steps.title: Copy each shard
steps.description: Replica A copies A, and replica B copies B. Replication supplies redundant copies rather than a new partition of the dataset.

steps.title: Place copies independently
steps.description: Each replica represents another storage instance. Use separate failure domains when resilience is the goal; copying onto the same failed machine would not help.

title: Cache-aside read paths
description: Choose a hit or a miss, then follow the application’s work.

steps.title: Check Redis
steps.description: The application looks up the profile key in the memory cache before querying the database.

steps.title: Hit: finish early
steps.description: If a usable cached value exists, return it to the caller. No database read is required on this branch.

steps.title: Miss: read durable storage
steps.description: If the key is absent or expired, the application queries the database. This is an alternative to the hit branch.

steps.title: Fill and return
steps.description: After a successful database read, the application writes the value to Redis with its chosen TTL and returns it. The upward connector represents application-coordinated cache population.

title: Delivery, commit and replay
description: An explicit consumer failure timeline, with offset commits as progress acknowledgments.

steps.title: Deliver record 42
steps.description: Assume the committed next offset is 42. The consumer fetches record 42 and performs its effect, such as storing downloaded HTML.

steps.title: Successful path: commit 43
steps.description: Only after successful processing, commit 43 as the next offset. This acknowledges consumer progress; it is separate from producer acknowledgment settings.

steps.title: Alternative: crash before commit
steps.description: If the effect succeeds but the consumer crashes before the commit, Kafka still records 42 as the next offset.

steps.title: Replay can repeat effects
steps.description: The replacement fetches 42 again. An idempotent effect or deduplication with a stable event ID prevents an unwanted duplicate effect.

steps.title: Processing errors need a policy
steps.description: Crash replay differs from retrying a processing error. A retry topic, backoff and eventual dead-letter handling require application logic.

title: BFS queue trace
description: Watch first discovery determine distance and prevent duplicate queue entries.

steps.title: Seed the source
steps.description: Set distance[A] to zero, mark A visited and enqueue it. The queue contains discovered but unprocessed vertices.

steps.title: Expand A
steps.description: Pop A, then discover B and C in that order. Mark each on enqueue and set both distances to one.

steps.title: Expand B
steps.description: Pop B. D is unvisited, so mark and enqueue D with distance two. C stays ahead of D in the FIFO queue.

steps.title: Expand C
steps.description: Pop C. Its neighbor D was marked when B discovered it, so D is not added a second time.

steps.title: Finish the layer
steps.description: Pop D. No unvisited neighbors remain and the queue empties. Every vertex was enqueued only once, in nondecreasing distance order.
